memoryReview.lesson: Avoid a grid puzzle, twin characters, and warehouse navigation; render one continuous robot journey.
Avoid realistic car damage and dashboard telemetry; keep a toy factory and tactile shared actions.
Do not mimic miniature golf courses or their camera; favor a side-on mechanical rail.
Avoid paper material, brush panels and painter metaphors.
Avoid abstract luminous trajectory effects; keep highly legible solid obstacle silhouettes.

references.observation: Compact hardware uses tactile, clearly separated controls and an exposed industrial casing.
references.principle: One action occupies one unmistakable physical button.
references.application: Two oversized mechanical plungers are the main mobile input.
references.avoid: Do not reproduce product layout, silkscreen labels, logo or distinctive branded electronics.

references.observation: The physical comedy comes from shared action and awkward movement while attempting a common objective.
references.principle: Consequences of player actions should be visible and physically grounded.
references.application: Launch timing creates jumps, falls and accidental retreat instead of separate scripted jokes.
references.avoid: No copying character art, ragdoll movement or level layout.

references.observation: Two players can share a short puzzle scenario with immediate cause and effect.
references.principle: Keep a single joint goal and readable shared information.
references.application: One visible finish, two role-specific controls and instant retries.
references.avoid: No paper cutting, protagonist silhouettes or Nintendo UI.

concepts.medium: Vector Canvas 2D and CSS-styled metal/plastic buttons.
concepts.composition: Full scene plus a two-channel bottom console.
concepts.interaction: Two operators independently pulse one shared autonomous robot.
concepts.motion: Sinking plungers, body angle and wheel rotation.
concepts.rationale: Best readability and originality at mobile aspect ratios.

concepts.medium: Single-color CRT traces and numerical console glyphs.
concepts.composition: Instrument display with data bands and tiny robot silhouette.
concepts.interaction: Timed waveform toggles adjust motor and jump.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because abstract waveform control hides the physical joke.

concepts.medium: Illustrated plush felt and chunky stitched toy accessories.
concepts.composition: Portrait dollhouse with scattered tabletop controls.
concepts.interaction: Pull fabric straps to redirect a soft robotic toy.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because cloth simulation and toy-craft styling conflict with immediate two-button mechanics.

selection.reason: A control-as-object interaction emphasizes both roles; a visually separate world remains readable on narrow devices.

rejected.reason: Too abstract to understand a jump collision at a glance.
Requires additional soft-body art and hides the mechanical plunger signature.

tools.reason: Canvas 2D is a built-in rendering interface; no external art runtime required.
The launcher icon and action glyphs are original authored SVG/CSS geometry.
No local Blender assets required for a two-dimensional side-view proof; could use a licensed future asset pipeline if changed.
tools.fallback: Use the existing original Canvas 2D geometry for the robot and factory instead of external Blender exports in this first playable stage.

assets.role: Main robot chassis, optics and wheels.
assets.acceptance: Clearly visible at mobile zoom and never confusable with static platforms.
assets.integration: Renderer consumes fixed-step state without mutating it.
assets.provenance: Original authored geometry in the app source.

assets.role: Operator action surfaces in amber and faded blue enamel.
assets.acceptance: Each touch target exceeds 44 CSS pixels with immediate pressed response.
assets.integration: Buttons dispatch jump/reverse to the local simulation.
assets.provenance: Original CSS shapes with text labels.

assets.role: Pocket Works launcher mark of a single amber pushbutton.
assets.acceptance: Readable at 48×48 and unique from other apps.
assets.provenance: Original SVG created for this app.

risks: On short phones the control deck can consume the scene's height.
The fixed timestep must not tunnel through a ledge after background suspension.
Camera should not lose the robot at the goal.
Sound should never autoplay before interaction.
comparisons: Initial menu to active side-scrolling world at 390×844.
Jump and wall collision compared with gap death and respawn.
Pause and successful finish without browser scrolling.
